title: Attestation-gated rollout playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for doing attestation-gated, staged rollouts of private deployments (VPC / on-prem clusters). It stitches together Terraform module expectations, image signing/attestation verification with cosign, a lightweight Argo/GitOps workflow for staged canaries, and the rollback/mitigation runbook.

Scope / non-goals:
- Scope: s2s private clusters that run Redwood Private (k8s + Helm) managed via ArgoCD and Terraform for infra. Focus on the release path from image build -> attestation -> GitOps promotion -> cluster rollout.
- Non-goals: full CI build pipelines, vendor-specific OS patching, or network provisioning beyond expected TF module inputs.

Assumptions:
- Images built in CI are signed and attested (cosign + Rekor) before publishing to the customer artifact registry.
- Customer clusters have an ArgoCD instance per environment or per tenant; we target a single Argo Application per installation.
- There is a Terraform module exposed to customers that provisions Kubernetes, VPC networking, and an Argo admin role binding (module outputs a cluster id and argocd kubeconfig secret name).
- KMS keys are available for image signing where required (we accept both vendor KMS and customer HSM-backed keys).

Quick glossary:
- Attestation: a signed statement (e.g., in in-toto format) asserting build provenance and policy checks.
- Gate: a check in the GitOps promotion pipeline that validates attestation before applying manifests to a target cluster.
- Canaries / staged rollout: progressive target groups (canary-1 -> canary-2 -> 50% -> 100%).

High-level flow (one-line):
1) CI builds image and produces cosign signature + attestation -> pushes to registry
2) CI creates a release PR in infra repo with image-tag bump + attestation metadata
3) Automated pre-merge validator checks attestation against policy (build toolchain id, SBOM, vuln threshold)
4) Merge -> GitOps pipeline (ArgoCD) picks up new revision but a promotion controller runs attestation verification before promoting to each stage
5) Staged rollout executed with smoke tests and metric checks at each step; failures trigger automatic rollbacks and alerting

Terraform module notes (interface expectations):
- Module: redwood-private-cluster (customer-facing) - keep inputs minimal for parity with hosted API. Example variables we expect and validate at release time:
  - cluster_name (string)
  - environment (string; one of dev,staging,prod)
  - argocd_admin_group (string)
  - image_registry_endpoint (string) - registry we will allow in attestation policy
  - allowed_image_signers (list of strings) - key ids (KMS/HSM) that are permitted to sign images
  - image_attestation_policy (string) - policy reference or inline policy id
  - enable_attestation_gate (bool)
Outputs we rely on in release automation:
  - argocd_app_namespace
  - argocd_repo_url (gitops manifest repo)
  - cluster_kubeconfig_secret_name
Notes / TODOs for module authors:
- Export a minimal claim in outputs so the release automation can target specific argocd apps (avoid wide permissions).
- Provide IAM role binding documentation snippets for teams with restricted RBAC.

Image signing / attestation verification (practical checks):
- Required pieces for verification step (CI or GitOps admission):
  - cosign signature present and verifiable against allowed public keys (or KMS key ids).
  - Rekor entry exists for immutability audit.
  - Attestation contents: builder id matches our canonical CI (or allowed builders list), SBOM attached or linked, vulnerability threshold not exceeded (e.g. high >=1 fails).
- Quick cosign verify command examples (ops cheatsheet):
  - cosign verify --attestation --key kms://projects/…/locations/…/keyRings/…/cryptoKeys/… gcr.io/customer/image:tag
  - cosign verify-attestation --cert <cert.pem> gcr.io/customer/image:tag
- When attestation is missing, do NOT auto-promote. The pipeline must either block and notify the release owner or fall back to a pre-approved exception process (PDEP-824).

Argo/GitOps promotion pattern (practical recipe):
- Repo layout (recommended):
  - gitops-repo/
    - clusters/
      - customer-a/
        - staging/
          - apps/
            - redwood-platform.yaml (Argo Application)
        - prod/
          - apps/
            - redwood-platform.yaml
- ArgoApp snippet (we keep the Argo side simple; the promotion logic lives in a small controller that checks attestation):
  - metadata.name: redwood-platform
    spec.source.repoURL: git@github.com:redwood-inference/gitops-manifests.git
    spec.source.targetRevision: refs/tags/RELEASE-2024-10-21
    spec.source.path: clusters/customer-a/prod/apps/redwood-platform
- Promotion controller responsibilities:
  - Before updating targetRevision for a next stage, fetch attestation metadata from the release PR and run verification (cosign + policy).
  - If verification succeeds, patch the Argo Application targetRevision for the next stage.
  - Post-patch, create a short-lived Argo Rollout (or Helm canary) config with traffic weights controlled by the controller.

Staged rollout plan (example steps):
- Stage names: canary-1 (1 pod), canary-2 (3 pods), ramp-50 (50% of nodes/traffic), full
- At each stage the controller runs the following checks within a configurable timeout (default 10m):
  - Pod readiness and startup latencies below threshold (p95 < 4s for our readiness probe)
  - Error rate (5xx) < 0.5% in canary group for the last 5m
  - Key user transaction latency (if available) p95 degrade < 15% vs baseline
  - Custom smoke test results (see smoke test section)
- Failure policy: immediate rollback to previous stable revision and open incident to #oncall-private-deploy with runbook link.

Smoke tests (simple verifiers to run after deploy):
- healthcheck endpoint returns 200 and expected payload keys
- basic prompt-generation flow (sample prompt per customer constraints) returns non-blank result within 2s median
- embedding endpoint (if relevant) returns vector length matching expected dims
- runny sample load: 5 qps across canary for 2m and assert error rate < 1%
- Implementation: use a small k8s job executed by the promotion controller (secrets pulled from the cluster k8s secret created by the Terraform module).

Rollback and mitigation steps (runbook):
1) Automated rollback triggered by controller: it patches the ArgoApp targetRevision back to the previous stable tag. Verify ArgoCD sync completes.
2) If automated rollback fails: open P1 with SRE + product on-call, scale down canary pods manually and block traffic at ingress (customer BGP/edge control or LB config).
3) Collect artifacts: pod logs, prometheus window (5m before to 5m after), envoy access logs, rollout history. Attach to Jira PDEP-824 if customer-impacting.

CI pipeline snippet (example GH Actions job simplified):
- name: build-and-attest
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: build image
      run: docker build -t $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$TAG .
    - name: push image
      run: docker push $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$TAG
    - name: cosign attest
      run: |
        cosign sign --key $COSIGN_KEY_REF $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$TAG
        cosign attest --predicate attestation.json --type in-toto --key $COSIGN_KEY_REF $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$TAG
    - name: create-release-pr
      run: |
        gh repo clone redwood-inference/gitops-manifests tmp && 
        cd tmp && 
        git checkout -b release/$TAG && 
        find . -type f -name 'redwood-platform.yaml' -exec sed -i 's|image: .*|image: $REGISTRY/$IMAGE:$TAG|' {} + && 
        git add . && git commit -m "release: bump image to $TAG (attested)" && git push origin release/$TAG && gh pr create --title "release: $TAG" --body "Attestation: $COSIGN_ATTESTATION_URL"

Gate exceptions and manual approvals:
- If attestation validation fails due to an allowed reason (e.g. SBOM generation failure), the release owner must create a documented exception ticket (JIRA PDEP-824) and request a one-time manual approval from the security reviewer. Approvals must be recorded in the PR and the controller must confirm PR has a recorded approval before allowing a manual bypass.

Operational runbook checklist (pre-rollout):
- [ ] Confirm cosign keys in allowed_image_signers match Terraform module outputs
- [ ] Verify Rekor is reachable from promotion controller environment
- [ ] Confirm ArgoApp points to a non-rolling tag (we prefer tags over floating refs)
- [ ] Create an incident channel; notify customer success for customer-impacting releases
- [ ] Confirm backup/restore snapshot schedule for cluster etcd is recent (within 24h)

Post-release verification (automated):
- daily job for 72h after prod rollout to check: crashloop restarts, OOM events, and a simple SLA test run. Any regression opens an auto-ticket.

Open questions / TODOs (research tasks):
- How to surface attestation metadata in the Argo UI easily? (Embed attestation URL in Argo Application annotations?)
- Define exact vulnerability threshold policy (current placeholder: fail on any HIGH)
- Decide whether to run attestation checks in a dedicated promotion-controller pod vs admission webhook on ArgoCD server. Tradeoffs: explicit control vs ARGO patch surface area.
- Add support for air-gapped customers where Rekor is unavailable (offline attestation caching strategy).

Appendix: quick debug commands for oncall
- Verify attestation locally: cosign verify --attestation --key <pubkey.pem> <image>
- Fetch Rekor entry: curl https://rekor.example.com/api/v1/log/entries?hash=<image-digest>
- Patch ArgoApp targetRevision: kubectl -n argocd patch application redwood-platform --type merge -p '{"spec":{"source":{"targetRevision":"RELEASE-2024-10-21"}}}'

Notes: this is a draft. Expect iterative changes as we pilot with 2 customers in Q1.

Unresolved: link to privilege escalation model for promotion controller (needs least-privilege iam role).
